articles.title: No, Digger Is Not a Misunderstood Masterpiece
articles.author: Eileen Jones
articles.content_excerpt: You may have heard already that Digger , the new film cowritten and directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu ( The Revenant, Birdman ) and starring Tom Cruise, is an expensive box-office bomb that got many annihilating reviews . One of the better ones sums it up perfectly: “It’s like being trapped inside a tuba for two hours.” Bad news travels fast. And I’m going to further speed it along by providing an all-spoiler review, so consider yourself warned. This is in order to convince you that you’d be better off staying home watching Dr. Strangelove , Stanley Kubrick’s scathingly funny and incisive 1964 protest against world-ending insanity, which set the template for satirical black comedy for generations to come. articles.title: Lula Is in Danger of Losing Brazil’s Presidency
articles.author: Aldo Cordeiro Sauda
articles.content_excerpt: The first round of Brazil’s elections dealt a heavy blow to the Workers’ Party (PT) and, more broadly, to the cause of democracy in Latin America. In 2022, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finished some six million votes ahead of Jair Bolsonaro in the first round, a margin that narrowed to about two million in the runoff. This time, Flávio Bolsonaro finished 2.2 million votes ahead of Lula, a lead of three percentage points. That makes the second round on October 25 especially difficult for Lula and the Brazilian left. The candidates who finished behind the top two, who together took around six million votes (roughly 6 percent), are all on the far right. articles.title: Richie Floyd: Bernie’s 2016 Campaign Changed My Life
articles.author: Richie Floyd
articles.content_excerpt: Bernie Sanders changed my life. And it happened overnight. Just over ten years ago, I was working as a hardware engineer. I grew up working class in the deeply conservative Florida Panhandle, where the Democratic Party had next to no foothold. The neoliberal ideas leading the conversation in the Democratic and Republican parties left me feeling disillusioned and unmoored from both the Left and the Right. I didn’t believe politics as it existed could have much of a positive impact on my life. While visiting with family at my parents’ house, I was asked by a friend if I had heard of Bernie Sanders. articles.title: Thomas Piketty’s Utopian Socialism
articles.author: Virgilio Urbina Lazardi
articles.content_excerpt: In June, the policy world held its collective breath as the World Inequality Lab, the outfit headed by Thomas Piketty , released a report meant to serve as a capstone to years of extensive research on the elusive goal of leveling global incomes. Christened the Global Justice Report ( GJR ), Piketty and his collaborators promoted it as the first data-driven synthesis of two long-standing progressive ambitions that had remained more aspirational than actionable: dramatically reducing income and wealth inequality both within countries and between them, on the one hand, and achieving planetary sustainability in the age of global warming, on the other. articles.title: Being Against Capitalism Isn’t Enough
articles.author: Mike Beggs
articles.content_excerpt: We live in a time when everything is political — except politics. We routinely treat everyday choices about culture, consumption, and personal identity as expressions of moral allegiance, parsing them for hidden meanings and assigning them to partisan camps. We infer entire worldviews from what people watch, buy, joke about, or post online. And yet, in this atmosphere of constant ideological conflict, the most fundamental political questions are almost never asked. How should an economy be organized? Are disparities in income and wealth intrinsically objectionable, or are they acceptable as long as no one is starving? Can political equality truly exist alongside economic inequality? articles.title: Spain’s New Protest Movement Is Putting Class Center Stage
articles.author: Paolo Gerbaudo
articles.content_excerpt: Fifteen years isn’t enough for a generation, but it seems it is the right amount of time for a “political cycle.” In Spain, activists and progressive academics have in recent years often spoken of the exhaustion of the political cycle that began with the Indignados protests, known as 15-M (so named after May 15, 2011, the first day of protest), and continued with the foundation of Podemos and its rapid growth, until the formation of the first broad-left coalition in 2019. This cycle has borne many results and led to a self-styled “progressive government” that presided over a period of steady economic growth. articles.title: Paris: Presentation of George Mavrikos’ book at the Bourse du Travail
articles.author: admin
articles.content_excerpt: On the joint initiative of the WFTU members in France and the International Workers’ Institute (IWI), the presentation of the book “Critical Notes on the History of the World Trade-Union Movement – Issues of Tactics and Strategy” took place on October 3 in Paris, at the Eugène Hénaff hall of the Paris Bourse du Travail. Speakers included Caroline Viau, Esteban Muñoz, Christoforos Giakoumelos, and Matthieu Bolle-Reddat, as well as the author of the book, George Mavrikos. A rich debate and interventions by the participants followed. The presentation coincided with the anniversary of the founding of the WFTU, which took place on October 3, 1945, in Paris. articles.title: Sanctuary for All
articles.author: Rochester Red Star: News from Rochester DSA
